thread_analysis.thread_summary: An internal Allion thread (entirely in English) coordinating Bluetooth RF PHY logo testing for an Alps Alpine UXC10 DUT at Allion's Taiwan HQ lab, between Toshitaka Mochizuki, lab engineer Leo Chou, Ning Lin, and Itsuo Sakai. The thread spans November 2025 through January 2026: test scheduling and rescheduling around sample readiness, a Test Plan correction (packet length error), test environment tooling setup (Qualcomm Package Manager, QRCT, QUTS Status App — similar to previously documented tooling issues in other Alinco/AlpsAlpine test threads), a DUT packet-length test anomaly (only testable at 37 bytes rather than the expected 255-byte maximum), and final report correction (date mismatch) through to test completion and customer delivery.
all_questions_found: (Raised but no explicit written resolution found in this thread) Why can the DUT only be tested with a 37-byte packet length instead of the expected 255-byte maximum specified for the Controller?
thread_analysis.key_technical_discussion: This thread's tooling setup issues (Qualcomm Package Manager/QRCT installation, missing QUTS Status App) closely mirror troubleshooting patterns already documented in other Alinco/Alps Alpine RF PHY test threads (see thread_0231, thread_0234, thread_0269) and are not repeated here as new cases. The DUT's packet-length test anomaly (37 bytes vs. expected 255) was escalated for internal advice but its resolution doesn't appear explicitly in the captured thread.
thread_analysis.key_decision_logic: Not applicable for the unresolved packet-length question; see referenced threads for the tooling setup decision logic.
thread_analysis.consulting_mistake: The DUT packet-length anomaly (testable only at 37 bytes vs. the expected 255-byte maximum) was escalated internally for advice but the written record doesn't capture an explicit resolution before the thread moves on to tooling setup and eventual test completion — a documentation gap worth flagging, similar to the unresolved multi-device question noted in thread_0256.
thread_analysis.consulting_takeaway: No new case files were created from this thread since its content substantially overlaps with already-documented test-tooling troubleshooting patterns from other threads; the unresolved packet-length anomaly is worth flagging for follow-up documentation if it recurs in future Alps Alpine UXC10-related testing.
